'''''Ahnfeltia plicata''''', the '''landlady's wig''', is a [[species]] of [[red alga]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Ahnfeltiaceae]]. It grows in northern parts of the [[Atlantic Ocean]].

==Description==
The landlady's wig forms tufted [[perennial plant]]s with wiry fronds, branching from a discoid holdfast. The cylindrical fronds branch and are [[terete]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Seaweeds of the British Isles|last1=Dixon|first1=Peter S.|last2=Irvine|first2=Linda M.|publisher=[[British Museum (Natural History)]]|year=1977|isbn=0-565-00781-5|volume=1 Rhodophyta}}</ref> they branch irregularly in a [[Dichotomy|dichotomous]] manner. Each plant is about {{convert|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide. The [[holdfast (biology)|holdfast]] is up to {{convert|2.5|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide and composed of a thin layer encrusting the rock [[Substrate (biology)|substrate]].<ref name="Surey">{{cite book|title=Seaweed: A user's guide|last1=Surey-Gent|first1=Sonia|last2=Morris|first2=Gordon|publisher=Whittet Books|year=1987|isbn=978-0-905483-60-3|location=London|pages=56–57}}</ref> The frond's reddish-black colour results from the red pigments [[phycoerythrin]] and [[phycocyanin]]. Their colour is so intense that it masks the presence of other pigments, [[chlorophyll a|chlorophyll ''a'']] and [[beta-Carotene]]. Some unique [[xanthophyll]]s are also present in this seaweed.<ref name=WoRMS/> The landlady's wig could be confused with ''[[Cordylecladia erecta]]'' but that species is less common and is thicker with more rigid, regularly branched fronds.<ref name=seaweedsite>{{cite web|url=http://www.seaweed.ie/descriptions/Ahnfeltia_plicata.php |title=''Ahnfeltia plicata'' (Hudson) Fries |work=The seaweed site |access-date=2012-09-06 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131001531/http://www.seaweed.ie/descriptions/Ahnfeltia_plicata.php |archive-date=2013-01-31 }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The landlady's wig is found on either side of the north Atlantic Ocean <ref name=seaweedsite/> from the middle shore down to depths of about {{convert|12|m}}. It grows on hard surfaces and is common on rock covered with sand and also occurs in [[Tide pool|rock pools]].<ref name=Marlin/> It is sometimes torn from the rock in storms, resulting in floating mats of weed. The base of the fronds continue to grow even when they are detached from their [[Holdfast (biology)|holdfast]]s.<ref name=Surey/>

==Biology==
The landlady's wig is a slow-growing species that may survive for five to ten years. It has different forms at different stages of its life cycle. On male plants there are [[Gametangium|spermatangial]] [[Sorus|sori]] that form swellings on the middle parts of the frond. On female plants there are [[gametangium|gametangial]] sori which are up to {{convert|5|mm}} long. After fertilization of the [[carpogonium]], [[carpospore]]s are formed on the female frond. These produce a second [[Ploidy|diploid]] generation, giving rise to a [[tetrasporophyte]] form that often encrusts pebbles. This produces [[tetraspore]]s which develop into new gametophyte plants.<ref name="Marlin">{{cite web|url=http://www.marlin.ac.uk/speciesfullreview.php?speciesID=2417|title=A red seaweed - ''Ahnfeltia plicata''|author=Rayment|first=Will|date=2004|work=[[Marine Life Information Network]] (MarLIN)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215111658/http://www.marlin.ac.uk/species/detail/1656|archive-date=2017-12-15|url-status=dead|access-date=2012-09-05}}</ref> The encrusting tetrasporophyte form is known as ''Porphyrodiscus simulans''.<ref name=seaweedsite/>

==Uses==
The landlady's wig is an [[edible seaweed]] and was used in the [[Soviet Union]] for the production of [[agar]]. It can also be eaten raw or cooked and is said to have a crunchy texture and pleasant taste.<ref name=Surey/>
